narr: Welcome to our English for Engineering course covering weeks 5 through 7. In this section, we'll explore rules, questions, and answers related to passive voice constructions and manufacturing processes.
Let's begin with some fundamental rules about active and passive voice constructions in English.

data.heading: Active vs. Passive Voice
bullets: The house wasn't being used by the owners during the winter.
The make-up artist has transformed the actor into a monster.
They hadn't owned the company for very long before they went bankrupt.
The photo was taken by my husband on the balcony of our hotel.

narr: In English, we can express actions in two ways: active voice and passive voice.
Let's look at some examples that demonstrate the difference between these constructions.
In the first sentence, we see a passive construction where the house undergoes the action of not being used.
The second sentence shows an active construction where the make-up artist performs the action of transforming the actor.
The third sentence is active, showing that the subjects performed the action of owning the company.
The final example is passive, with the photo undergoing the action of being taken.

data.heading: Activity 1 — Answer Key
data.problem: Choose the correct active or passive construction for each sentence.
steps: are being made
inspired — the story performs the action, so the active is correct
hasn't been inhabited
is set
will be shot
aren't recording — the actors perform the action (active)

narr: Now let's work through Activity 1, where we identify the correct active or passive construction.
For the first item, the correct answer is 'are being made' - a passive construction.
The second item requires the active form 'inspired' because the story performs the action.
For the third sentence, we use the passive perfect 'hasn't been inhabited'.
The fourth answer is 'is set' - a passive construction.
The fifth item uses the future passive 'will be shot'.
For the sixth sentence, we need the active form 'aren't recording' because the actors perform the action.

data.heading: Activity 1 — Answer Key (cont.)
steps: wasn't being used
has transformed — the make-up artist performs the action (active)
hadn't owned — active
was taken
data.result: The correct answers show when to use active or passive voice based on whether the subject performs or undergoes the action.

narr: The seventh answer is the passive continuous 'wasn't being used'.
The eighth item requires the active perfect 'has transformed' since the make-up artist performs the action.
For the ninth sentence, we use the active perfect 'hadn't owned'.
The final answer is the simple passive 'was taken'.

data.heading: Rule of Thumb for Voice Choice
bullets: Choose the passive when the subject undergoes the action and the doer is unknown or unimportant (Rules 1–2)
Keep the active when the subject performs the action on an object (Rule 7)

narr: Remember this important rule of thumb when choosing between active and passive voice.
First, choose the passive voice when the subject undergoes the action and the doer is unknown or unimportant.
Second, keep the active voice when the subject performs the action on an object.

data.heading: Activity 2 — Complete with the Passive
data.problem: Complete with the passive so that the meaning is the same. Only use 'by' if necessary.
steps: A lot of foreign films are subtitled.
Love in the Time of Cholera was written in 1985.
My laptop is being repaired at the moment.
The DVD of the film hasn't been released yet.
The film won't be finished until the spring.
The tickets have to be collected from the box office.

narr: Now let's practice transforming active sentences into passive constructions in Activity 2.
For the first item, 'They subtitle a lot of foreign films' becomes 'A lot of foreign films are subtitled' in passive voice.
The second sentence transforms to 'Love in the Time of Cholera was written in 1985' using the simple past passive.
For the third item, we use the present continuous passive: 'My laptop is being repaired at the moment'.
The fourth answer uses the present perfect passive: 'The DVD of the film hasn't been released yet'.
The fifth item requires the future passive: 'The film won't be finished until the spring'.
For the sixth sentence, we use the passive with 'have to': 'The tickets have to be collected from the box office'.

data.heading: Activity 2 — Complete with the Passive (cont.)
steps: The actor hadn't been told about the changes in the script.
La La Land was directed by Damien Chazelle.
The soundtrack has already been recorded.
The director was being interviewed about the film.
data.result: Note the tenses: present simple (1), past simple (2, 8), present continuous (3), present perfect (4, 9), will (5), have to (6), past perfect (7), past continuous (10). 'By' is only necessary in (8), where the director's name is the point of the sentence.

narr: The seventh answer uses the past perfect passive: 'The actor hadn't been told about the changes in the script'.
The eighth item includes 'by' because the director's name is important: 'La La Land was directed by Damien Chazelle'.
For the ninth sentence, we use the present perfect passive: 'The soundtrack has already been recorded'.
The final answer uses the past continuous passive: 'The director was being interviewed about the film'.

data.title: Week 5 Lecture
data.subtitle: Part 2: Listening and Oral Expression — Manufacturing Processes

narr: Moving on to Week 5 Lecture, Part 2, which focuses on listening and oral expression related to manufacturing processes.
We'll examine various manufacturing processes and their descriptions.

data.heading: Task 1 — Match Pictures with Descriptions
data.problem: Match each picture with its correct description. The ten pictures are labeled with process names: bolting, casting, drilling, inspection, painting, pressing, punching, turning, welding, and one other.
steps: A hole is made using a drill. → drilling
A surface is covered with paint. → painting
A hole is punched in a material. → punching
The work is checked carefully. → inspection
A surface is polished to make it smooth and shiny. → polishing
A material is pressed into the correct shape. → pressing

narr: In Task 1, we need to match each picture with its correct description of a manufacturing process.
The first description matches the drilling process, where a hole is made using a drill.
The second description corresponds to painting, where a surface is covered with paint.
The third description matches punching, where a hole is punched in a material.
The fourth description matches inspection, where the work is checked carefully.
The fifth description corresponds to polishing, where a surface is made smooth and shiny.
The sixth description matches pressing, where a material is shaped by pressure.

data.heading: Task 1 — Match Pictures with Descriptions (cont.)
steps: Hot liquid material is poured into a container and cooled to make the correct shape. → casting
Two pieces are joined together using very high temperature. → welding
A material is turned on a machine called a lathe. Part of the material is removed to make the correct shape. → turning
Two pieces are joined together using a nut and a bolt. → bolting
data.result: All ten pictures have been correctly matched with their descriptions based on the manufacturing processes they represent.

narr: The seventh description corresponds to casting, where liquid material is poured and cooled.
The eighth description matches welding, where pieces are joined with high temperature.
The ninth description corresponds to turning, where material is shaped on a lathe.
The final description matches bolting, where pieces are joined with a nut and bolt.
